runtime_candidates.interface_evidence: tools/llama-bench/README.md, tools/llama-bench/llama-bench.cpp, and common/arg.cpp at the pinned revision; reverified 2026-09-05
runtime_candidates.cpu_only_policy: Adapter always supplies -ngl 0 and --device none, strips inherited LLAMA_ARG_* and HF_* option environment variables before subprocess execution, then rejects any result that does not report n_gpu_layers=0 and devices=none.
runtime_candidates.network_policy: The repository-owned profile uses only an already-present local artifact path. Direct model URL, Docker repository, Hugging Face provider-acquisition, and RPC CLI flags are prohibited by profile validation, including equals forms. Inherited LLAMA_ARG_* / HF_* environment option surfaces are removed before subprocess execution so upstream environment parsing cannot re-enable acquisition, RPC, device, or GPU-layer paths.
runtime_candidates.artifact_identity_policy: The local artifact SHA-256 must match LoadRequest before READY and is revalidated immediately before every benchmark process. Observed post-load disappearance or hash mutation is rejected before process launch. This is a pre-launch fail-closed check and does not claim filesystem-level atomicity across a separate executable opening the path.

runtime_candidates.reason: Release 0.10.5 remains the latest published release as reverified on 2026-09-05, and current repository code search exposes no llamafile-bench entry point. Historical benchmark-interface claims are not promoted to current T030 authority.

decision: Reconcile and security-harden the historical profile-driven portable CPU benchmark adapter onto exact current main using the proven llama-bench interface. Force device=none, revalidate local artifact identity immediately before each process, remove inherited upstream option environment surfaces, prohibit direct model URL, Docker, Hugging Face provider, and RPC acquisition paths, and do not manufacture a llamafile adapter until a current stable interface is evidenced.
